channel.title: East & Inner with Ollie
channel.description: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern ear. No jargon. No mysticism. Just the real stuff — from the Huangdi Neijing to your morning coffee. Hosted by Ollie, a screech owl with a yin-yang pendant and a lot of questions. New episodes every other week.
channel.itunes:author: Ollie
channel.itunes:summary: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern ear. No jargon. No mysticism. Just the real stuff — from the Huangdi Neijing to your morning coffee.

item.title: Yin & Yang ≠ Good vs Evil
item.description: The biggest mistranslation in the history of wellness culture: Yin and Yang are NOT good and evil. In this first episode, Ollie walks you through the seesaw, the three rules nobody told you, and why you should stop driving nails through your internal balance. Plus: what Huangdi Neijing actually says about dynamic equilibrium. Featuring real guqin music by High Mountains Flowing Water.
item.itunes:summary: Yin and Yang are not good and evil. Ollie explains the seesaw, the three rules, and why you should stop fighting your body and start listening to it. Featuring guqin music.

item.title: Stop Fighting, Start Warming
item.description: When a cold hits, your first instinct is to fight it. But Chinese medicine says that's exactly the wrong move. Discover the three warming herbs — Gui Zhi, Gan Jiang, and Fu Zi — and learn why your body doesn't need a warrior. It just needs a blanket.
item.itunes:summary: Stop fighting colds. Start warming your body. Ollie explains the three warming herbs, the terrain theory, and why Gui Zhi Tang opens the Shanghan Lun. Featuring guqin music.

item.title: The Fire Inside You Is Going Out
item.description: You're always cold. Bone-tired. Told everything is normal. Classical Chinese medicine has a name for this: the Life Gate Fire — Ming Men — is flickering. Ollie explains Zhang Zhongjing's warming formulas, what blows out your internal flame, and how to gently coax it back. Featuring guqin music.
item.itunes:summary: Always cold and exhausted? Your Life Gate Fire may be fading. Ollie explains Ming Men, Zhang Zhongjing's warming wisdom, and how to restart your body's furnace.
